hook: Pat Gelsinger spent thirty years at Intel, from 1979 to 2009, where he became the company's first chief technology officer, then ran EMC as president and COO and VMware as CEO before returning to lead Intel as chief executive from 2021 to 2024. Since March 2025 he has been a general partner at the venture firm Playground Global and executive chair and head of technology at Gloo, and he chairs or sits on the boards of several chip and compute startups. His LinkedIn profile credits him with helping create USB and Wi-Fi.

quick_facts: Worked at Intel from October 1979 to September 2009 in engineering and executive roles, ending as senior vice president and general manager of the Digital Enterprise Group, according to his LinkedIn profile
Intel's first chief technology officer, January 2000 to January 2005, per his profile
President and COO of EMC from September 2009 to August 2012, and CEO of VMware from September 2012 to February 2021
CEO of Intel from February 2021 to December 2024, and chairman of Mobileye from October 2022 to December 2024, leading its board through its return to public markets
General Partner at Playground Global and Executive Chair and Head of Technology at Gloo since March 2025
Member of the National Academy of Engineering, IEEE Fellow and author of The Juggling Act

achievements.title: Lead architect, Intel 80486 (1985-1989)
achievements.impact: The first Intel processor to exceed one million transistors, foundational to the PC era.

achievements.title: Intel's first CTO (2000-2005)
achievements.impact: Set technology direction across Intel's product lines. His profile also says he helped create USB and Wi-Fi, a claim this page attributes to him.

achievements.title: CEO of VMware (2012-2021)
achievements.impact: Grew VMware into a cloud-infrastructure leader before its acquisition by Broadcom.

achievements.title: Return as Intel CEO and the IDM 2.0 strategy (2021-2024)
achievements.impact: Launched Intel Foundry Services and multi-billion-dollar U.S. fab investments aimed at restoring domestic chip manufacturing capacity for the AI era.

achievements.title: Investor and board chair in AI hardware (2025 to present)
achievements.impact: General Partner at Playground Global, chairman of Snowcap Compute and xLight, and a board member at Ayar Labs, Powerlattice Technologies, Alva Energy, Vertical Semiconductor and Syenta.

source_basis: Updated 2026-10-23 from Pat Gelsinger's LinkedIn profile, supplied as a PDF by the editor on 2026-10-22. The USB and Wi-Fi credit is his own claim. The Intel biography page the bridge row names refused our request, so nothing was taken from it.

editor_points.desc: Thirty years at Intel from October 1979 to September 2009 in engineering and executive roles, ending as senior vice president and general manager of the Digital Enterprise Group. Intel's first ever CTO, January 2000 to January 2005. His profile says he helped create USB and Wi-Fi.
editor_points.name: Intel, 1979 to 2009

editor_points.desc: President and COO of EMC, September 2009 to August 2012. CEO of VMware, September 2012 to February 2021.
editor_points.name: EMC and VMware

editor_points.desc: CEO of Intel from February 2021 to December 2024. Chairman of Mobileye from October 2022 to December 2024, leading the board through its return to public markets.
editor_points.name: Intel CEO and Mobileye

editor_points.desc: Since March 2025, General Partner at Playground Global and Executive Chair and Head of Technology at Gloo in Boulder.
editor_points.name: Playground Global and Gloo

editor_points.desc: Chairman of Snowcap Compute (June 2025) and xLight (March 2025). Board member at Syenta (March 2026), Vertical Semiconductor (January 2026), Ayar Labs (November 2025), Alva Energy (August 2025) and Powerlattice Technologies (May 2025). Advisor to the National Security Telecommunications Advisory Committee since March 2020 and chairman of Transforming the Bay with Christ since 2014.
editor_points.name: Boards

editor_points.desc: Member of the National Academy of Engineering and IEEE Fellow. Author of The Juggling Act. Honorary doctorates from Taylor University (November 2025), Technion (May 2025) and Carnegie Mellon (May 2023), and doctorates from Ohio State (2022) and Indiana Wesleyan (2021).
